claim_being_audited: The model can be certified for launch based on aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, with the disability accommodations intake gap handled as a documented limitation plus post-launch monitoring.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the certification satisfies the release policy threshold.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
For a material limitation in a named launch use case, admissible evidence must show resolution, required disclosure, or approved risk acceptance before launch.
Absent that support link, certification is not evidentially supported even if aggregate readiness metrics are favorable.
evidence_requests: Evidence of the final legal determination on whether the disability accommodations intake gap must be disclosed before launch.
Evidence that the limitation was disclosed in the model card or equivalent launch documentation for the named use case.
Evidence of approved risk acceptance specifically covering this named launch use case limitation before launch.
Evidence that the segment gap has been remediated and now meets target, if the actor wants to rely on resolution instead of disclosure or risk acceptance.
specific_concerns: The admissible record shows a target miss in the disability accommodations intake segment, and that segment is named in two university accommodation commitments, which makes the weakness material under the stated policy.

The policy says material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, but no disclosure decision, approved risk acceptance, or remediation closure is in evidence.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure or risk-acceptance requirement for a material named-use-case limitation.
The product note calling the segment non-core because of projected traffic does not resolve materiality under the policy text.
unsupported_claims: That certification is policy-compliant on the current record.
That recording the segment gap as a tracked limitation is sufficient in place of required disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance.
That aggregate pass and rehearsal stability are enough to clear launch despite the unresolved material limitation.
